name: Powers House

dates.note: Four sources read the same day give 1903 — the Lanterman House's Haley building list ('The Powers House, built in 1903'), Allard Real Estate, Los Angeles Relics and Big Orange Landmarks — while the style node's exemplar carries 1904. Both are recorded; the exemplar's year was NOT changed.

refs.title: Alvarado Terrace Historic District, National Register reference No. 84000783, added 17 May 1984 — a DISTRICT listing covering the whole street, of which this house is one contributing property; the house carries no individual National Register number
No. 86 - Powers House (Los Angeles Historic-Cultural Monument No. 86)
refs.note: '1345 Alvarado Terrace. This Mission Revival home was built by and for Pomeroy W. Powers.'

refs.title: Haley Building List — Lanterman House
refs.note: The architect's own catalogue raisonne, kept by another Haley building's museum: 'The Powers House, built in 1903, was commissioned by Pomeroy W. Powers and his wife Ida. The Mission Revival-style home is stucco on frame construction. It still stands in Alvarado Terrace and is Los Angeles City Historical-Cultural Monument #86.'

refs.title: Pico Union Walking Tour Brochure — Los Angeles Conservancy
refs.note: 'Today, the Powers Residence is known as Casa San Juan Diego', run by the Missionaries of Charity Brothers; 'Alvarado Terrace was listed as a National Register Historic District in 1984.'

note: Seeded 5 Sep 2026 as the node's ordinary house — the case where Mission Revival is a builder's idiom rather than a monument. The Haley list's 'stucco on frame construction' is the single construction statement any source makes about it and there is no survey to measure. NOTE for the one-building-one-record guard: the National Register number here belongs to the DISTRICT and not to this house, and its title says so; it may legitimately be shared with any other contributing property that gets a record.
